sources.title: Comparative Analysis of Distributed Caching Algorithms: Performance ...
sources.snippet: Our comparative analysis reveals that while traditional algorithms like LRU and LFU continue to serve as foundational approaches in distributed caching, hybrid and adaptive algorithms demonstrate superior performance across diverse workload patterns.

sources.title: PDF Evaluating Cache-Replacement Policies Under a Mixed Workload
sources.snippet: Objective This report evaluates three cache-replacement policies — LRU (Least Recently Used), LFU (Least Frequently Used) and CLOCK — on a simulated single-level cache under a workload that mixes a scanning access pattern with a small set of hot keys. The goal is to identify which policy best resists cache pollution from the scan.

sources.title: Cache Eviction Algorithms: LRU vs LFU vs S3-FIFO
sources.snippet: One million requests per pattern, four eviction algorithms, code included: LRU hit exactly 0% on loops, and S3-FIFO led 8 of 12 hit-rate tests overall.

sources.title: No-Regret Mixing of LRU and LFU with Optimal Switching Cost
sources.snippet: Caching systems often rely on simple eviction policies such as Least Recently Used (LRU) and Least Frequently Used (LFU), which perform well in complementary request regimes. Recent policies such as LeCar and Cacheus combine LRU and LFU using ideas from the experts problem in online learning. Specifically, upon a miss, they randomize between the two eviction rules using probabilities derived from scores updated by tracking the history of past evictions.
